pv-price.reason: Opens on Price's biography and platform; what he named (the Church's consent to slavery) and the Word's weighing (no respecter of persons) sit mid-paragraph; ends on why he is placed first.
pv-price.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What did Frederick K.C. Price dare to name in 1997, and how does the Word weigh it? He named the American Church's own part in racism and slavery: that it "sided with evil rather than the Word of God". The Word weighs that charge and finds it true, because Yahweh shows no partiality between peoples, so a Church that blessed the subjugation of a race betrayed its own Lord. Here is the record.
pv-price.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What did Price name, and how does the Word weigh it? He said plainly, from inside the house and at real cost, that "Slavery could never have existed without the consent of the Church." Set beside Acts 10:34-35, Galatians 3:28 and James 2:1, the charge holds: Yahweh favors no race, all are one in Christ Jesus, and partiality in the assembly is sin. So the Word does not soften his words. It confirms them, and it calls the Church to that same plain honesty now.

teen.open: In 1997 a famous pastor, Frederick K.C. Price, said the American Church helped make slavery possible. Was he right? The Bible says Yahweh treats every people the same, so yes.
teen.close: So Price told the truth. Yahweh has no favorite race, and a church that blessed slavery went against its own Lord. Saying that out loud took courage.

senior.open: In 1997 Dr. Frederick K.C. Price charged the American Church with consenting to slavery. Weighed by the Word, which says Yahweh is no respecter of persons, the charge stands.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. Price named the Church's complicity at cost to himself, and Scripture confirms him: Yahweh favors no race, and partiality in His house is sin.

pv-darby.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why does a teacher like Stephen Darby get resisted, and why must the record be kept honest? Because the one who names a people's sin has always been resisted and sent away, from Stephen in Acts 7 to Amos. And because a true record must be true in every line, we keep what is sourced apart from what is only a reading, and we weigh each message by the Word.
pv-darby.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why is a voice like Darby's resisted? Because he teaches what most pulpits avoid, and the one who names a people's sin has always met resistance: Stephen stoned, Amos told to flee, the prophet without honour in his own country. Why keep the record honest? So it can stand. His ministry, dates and titles are sourced; the claims about why he was overlooked are labeled as Darrell's framing; and every teaching is weighed by the Word. Kept that way, the record can be trusted.

teen.open: People who name a nation's sin usually get pushed away. Pastor Stephen Darby teaches hard things, and this lesson shows why that brings pushback.
teen.close: So prophets get resisted because they say what people do not want to hear. We keep his record honest by checking the facts and testing his teaching by the Word.

senior.open: Those who name a people's sin have always been resisted, from Stephen in Acts to Amos. Pastor Stephen Darby stands in that pattern, which is why his record must be kept carefully and honestly.
senior.close: The answer, then, is twofold. Such voices are resisted because they name sin plainly, and the record stays honest by separating sourced fact from framing and weighing every teaching by the Word.

pv-diop.reason: Answers the title only implicitly: the methods are listed mid-paragraph, the Luke 8:17 light frame comes near the end, and the yes-it-outlasts answer is left to the last clause.
pv-diop.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Could a scientist's evidence outlast the silence? Yes. Cheikh Anta Diop refused to let the question of whether Kemet (ancient Egypt) was African be settled by assumption, and he tested it with the tools of science. The room in Cairo in 1974 largely closed against him, but Yahweh's Word promises that nothing hidden stays hidden, so honest evidence keeps coming back to the light.
pv-diop.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Could his evidence outlast the silence? It has. Diop built a radiocarbon laboratory, measured, tested and mapped where others only presumed, and he stood almost alone at the UNESCO Symposium. We keep his record honestly: his methods and the Symposium are documented, and the debated conclusions are named as debated. And over the silence stands the promise of Luke 8:17 and the prayer of Psalm 43:3. Evidence that welcomes scrutiny does not stay buried. Yahweh's light brings it back.

teen.open: Can good evidence win even when people ignore it? Cheikh Anta Diop tested a big claim about ancient Egypt with science instead of guessing, and the answer is yes.
teen.close: So yes, the evidence can outlast the silence. Diop tested instead of assuming, and the Word says nothing hidden stays hidden forever.

senior.open: Dr. Cheikh Anta Diop tested, by science, a claim others had merely presumed: that Kemet was not truly African. He was not heard in his day, yet his evidence has outlasted that silence.
senior.close: So the answer is yes. Honest testing, kept honest about what is still debated, is the kind of record that Yahweh's light brings back, for nothing hidden stays hidden (Luke 8:17).

pv-inventions.reason: States early that patent law barred enslaved inventors and enslavers took the credit (Latimer vs Edison as proof), and ends squarely on Proverbs 22:22-23: Yahweh takes the side of the robbed.

pv-williams.reason: The two causes (outside invasion, inside disunity) arrive mid-lesson; the link to the Church (one body, many members) is one clause; the ending lands on rebuilding, not on the Church today.
pv-williams.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What did Chancellor Williams learn about division, and why does it matter for the Church? He found that a people is destroyed two ways: from without, by invasion, and from within, by disunity. His law is plain: unity is strength, division is vulnerability. That matters for the Church because we are told we are one body with many members, so his mirror convicts us too.
pv-williams.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What did Williams learn, and why does it matter for the Church today? An enemy at the gate can only exploit a division that is already inside. He held that mirror up to his own people, and it fits the Body of Christ just as well, because "if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand" (Mark 3:25). So the Church recovers the hidden knowledge, refuses the division, and pays whatever the truth costs. That is how a people rebuilds instead of only mourning.

teen.open: A historian named Chancellor Williams found that a people can be destroyed by enemies outside and by splits inside. The Church can be too.
teen.close: So the lesson is simple. Unity is strength and division is weakness. A church that stays united can stand and rebuild.

senior.open: Dr. Chancellor Williams concluded that destruction comes both from without and from within, and that disunity is what leaves a people open. The same truth speaks to the Church.
senior.close: That is why his work matters for believers today. A house divided cannot stand (Mark 3:25), and a Body that refuses division and buys the truth is able to rebuild.

pv-obenga.reason: The test (systematic sound, symbol and meaning correspondences) is described mid-paragraph, and why truth outlasts (a lying tongue is but for a moment) only arrives near the end.
pv-obenga.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What does Dr. Obenga's case ask us to test? Whether ancient Egyptian is kin to the languages of Black Africa, judged by systematic matches in sound, symbol and meaning, not by slogans. And why does truth outlast a forged story? Because a ruler can carve a false history on a wall, but the deep kinship of a language is very hard to fake.
pv-obenga.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What are we asked to test, and why does truth outlast the forgery? We test the correspondences Obenga set out, KMT becoming Kemet, NTR becoming Neter, MAA carried across the centuries, while holding his "Negro-Egyptian" proposal as his argued claim, still contested, not settled fact. And we trust the outcome to the Word: "The lip of truth shall be established for ever: but a lying tongue is but for a moment" (Proverbs 12:19). The forged story is temporary. The truth carried in the tongue endures.

teen.open: Dr. Obenga studied languages to see if ancient Egypt's tongue was related to Black African languages. Words can carry truth for a very long time.
teen.close: So we test his word matches honestly, without calling them settled. And the Bible says the truth lasts forever while a lie lasts only a moment.

senior.open: Dr. Théophile Obenga asks us to test whether ancient Egyptian is genetically kin to the languages of Black Africa, by careful correspondences of sound, symbol and meaning.
senior.close: His proposal is weighed honestly as a contested claim, yet the principle stands: the lip of truth is established for ever, and a lying tongue is but for a moment (Proverbs 12:19).
